question.leadin: On March 29, 1960, the New York Times published a full-page ad seeking support for Martin Luther King and civil rights in the south called "Heed Their Rising Voices."
question.text: The ad was signed by dozens of activists, including this future Chairman of SNCC ["snick"] who was badly beaten on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in 1965. This man served in the House, representing Georgia, until his July 2020 death.
question.clue: This former Representative from Georgia who as head of SNCC ["snick"] helped organize the 1963 March on Washington. With Katherine Clarke, he led a Congressional sit-in to demand gun control legislation after the Pulse nightclub shooting.

swap.text: This lawyer successfully argued Brown before the Supreme Court. He became the first African-American justice on the Supreme Court in 1967.
swap.clue: Earlier, he argued for the winning side of the Supreme Court cases Smith v. Allwright and Sweatt v. Painter.

question.leadin: This man declared "segregation now, segregation tomorrow, segregation forever," then tried to back that up by standing in the door to block two black students from entering his state's university in Tuscaloosa.
question.text: Name this politician. His wife, Lurleen, ran for governor when he was term-limited in 1966.
question.clue: This man considered Colonel Sanders as a running mate for one campaign, but ultimately chose nuclear weapons enthusiast Curtis Lemay.

swap.text: King led this organization that fought to end segregation. He founded it with Ralph Abernathy after the Montgomery Bus boycott, and it led a march on Washington.
swap.clue: At that time it had been led for four years by Ralph David Abernathy after the death of its founder.

question.leadin: The speaker of this speech quotes "My Country Tis of Thee" for a desire to sing with a new meaning: "from every mountainside, let freedom ring!"
question.text: Name this speech in which the speaker wishes that allowing Freedom to ring would speed up the day that all of God's children can join hands and sing "free at last."
question.clue: The beginning of this speech states that "Five score years ago, a great American, in whose symbolic shadow we stand, signed the Emancipation Proclamation."

swap.leadin: This policy was at the center of the case Grutter v. Bollinger.
swap.text: Name this policy central to the similar Gratz v. Bollinger, which ruled unconstitutional a points-based college admissions approach.
swap.answerHtml: affirmative action [or race-based affirmative action; prompt on racial balancing or non-race-blind admissions or racial quotas or other descriptions of taking race into account in school admissions]
swap.clue: In another case involving this concept, the Supreme Court rejected the logic of "business necessity," and allowed the implementation of this concept on the basis of statistical evidence.

question.leadin: Name some landmark U.S. court cases.
question.text: This 1963 case dealt with a Florida man convicted of breaking into the Bay Harbor Pool Room and ruled that not giving a convicted felon a right to counsel was unconstitutional.
question.clue: Future Supreme Court Justice Abe Fortas was appointed to represent the plaintiff in this case, who was arrested in Panama City, Florida for breaking into a pool hall.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about US health care reform in the 20th century.
swap.text: This series of domestic reforms introduced Medicare and Medicaid.
swap.answerHtml: Great Society [prompt on descriptive answers such as Lyndon Baines Johnson's social reforms]
swap.clue: One act under this program significantly boosted public education funding, while another created the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

question.leadin: It established the principle requiring "actual malice" for a libel claim by a public figure.
question.text: Name this 1964 Supreme Court case arising out of a newspaper ad attacking members of the Alabama government for suppressing civil rights demonstrations.
question.answerHtml: New York Times v. Sullivan [or Sullivan v. New York Times]
question.clue: This case established the actual malice rule, requiring proof of "reckless disregard" in order to sue a newspaper for defamation or libel.

swap.text: This mayor from 1955 to 1976, who shares his first and last name with his son who has been mayor since 1989, controlled the Democratic "Organization," which used patronage and boss-style politics to rule the city.
swap.clue: This man ordered police to "shoot to kill" during the MLK riots, the same year his "Gestapo tactics" were condemned by Abraham Ribicoff.

question.leadin: Identify these people and organizations involved in the Civil Rights movement.
question.text: As field director for the NAACP in Mississippi, this man was conducting a voter registration drive when assassinated in 1963.
question.clue: This D-Day veteran, who tried to integrate his state's public law school in 1954.

swap.leadin: This man was murdered in 1978 by fellow city supervisor Dan White, who later argued he had been crazed by a sugar rush from a Twinkie.
swap.text: Who was this first openly gay elected official in California, played by Sean Penn in an eponymous bio-pic?
swap.clue: This man's death inspired Cleve Jones to begin the NAMES Project.

question.text: This Baptist minister led protests after the Diallou shootings. This MSNBC commentator ran in the 2004 Democratic Primary, memorably asking Howard Dean in a debate whether he employed Black people on his staff.

swap.leadin: Workers in this industry striked under the slogan "I AM a Man."
swap.text: Name this industry, whose workers began striking in response to the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. Martin Luther King Jr. was in Memphis supporting the strike in this industry in 1968 when he was assassinated.
swap.answerHtml: sanitation industry [or garbagemen; or any other answers suggesting garbage collection; or Memphis sanitation strike]
swap.clue: This industry's use of "wiener barrel" trucks declined after Echol Cole and Robert Walker's deaths triggered a strike that popularized the slogan "I AM A MAN."

question.text: The exclusion of women at the march was protested by this African-American feminist, who had been arrested in 1970 for purchasing a shotgun used in an escape attempt by the Soledad Brothers, though she was acquitted.
question.clue: This former UCLA professor and member of the Black Panthers was put on trial for her alleged role in the attempted kidnapping of Judge Howard Haley at a Marin County courthouse.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about photographs of people dying in different ways.
swap.text: This photographer won the 1976 Pulitzer and the World Press Photo of the Year for his shot of two girls tumbling from the fifth story of a building in "Fire Escape Collapse." He won another Pulitzer the next year for "The Soiling of Old Glory."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Supreme Court cases originating in Ohio.
question.text: In this 1968 case, Earl Warren's court held that a police ofcer does not violate the Fourth Amendment by frisking a sus-pect without probable cause, if the ofcer has a reasonable suspicion that the suspect is armed and dangerous or involved in criminal activity.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about some common occurrences in New York City.
swap.text: Edward Shapiro called this riot, lasting from August 19-22, 1991, the "most serious anti-Semitic incident in American history". It takes its name from the heavily-Caribbean Brooklyn neighborhood where it took place.
swap.clue: Lemnick Nelson was accused of stabbing an Australian graduate student during it, and it was touched off when the leading car of a motorcade killed a seven year old boy named Gavin Cato.

question.text: Titles VIII and IX of the 1968 Civil Rights Act, which was signed during the riots, are commonly named for this issue. The Ink for Jack campaign arose from JFK's failure to use a "stroke of the pen" to address this issue, which was the focus of the Chicago Freedom Movement.
question.answerHtml: housing discrimination [accept fair housing or open housing; accept housing anti-discrimination; accept Fair Housing Act; prompt on descriptions of discrimination in the sale or rental of dwelling places; reject “public housing” or “affordable housing”]

swap.leadin: Section 2 of this act was the subject of the case Bartlett v. Strickland, while a 2009 Supreme Court ruling provided more leeway for statesto subvert its pivotal Section 5, but declined to rule on that section's constitutionality. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this legislation, whose major requirement for specifically identified areas to gain "preclearance" from the Justice Department remains enforced. It was also the subject of the "King Letter" over its sections involving multilingualism.
swap.clue: Among the provisions of this legislation was a triggering clause that required federal pre-clearance of procedural changes.
